locate_file <- function(fn, path = ".", tar_fn=NULL, custom_message=NULL) {
  # locate filename
  fn_full = list.files(path = path, pattern = fn, full.names = TRUE) # locate Rdata object containing res.rank
  # determine if file is missing
  if (!is.null(custom_message)) {
    if (length(fn_full) != 1) stop(custom_message)
  } else {
    if (is.null(tar_fn)) {tar_fn_text=""} else {tar_fn_text=glue(" {tar_fn}")}
    if (length(fn_full) == 0) stop(glue("Tarfile{tar_fn_text} is missing expected file '{fn}'. \nTar Dir:{tar_dir}\nLS:{paste0(list.files(tar_dir), collapse='\n')}"))#\n\nLS:{paste0(list.files(file.path(tar_dir,'cmap')), collapse='\n')}))
    if (length(fn_full) > 1) stop(glue("Tarfile{tar_fn_text} contains more than one file matching '{fn}' filename."))
  }
  # return filename
  return(fn_full)
}

# Convert PDF plots to PNG for reliable HTML rendering.
prepare_figure_for_html <- function(path, dpi = 200) {
  if (tolower(tools::file_ext(path)) != "pdf") return(path)

  png_path <- sub("\\.[Pp][Dd][Ff]$", ".png", path)
  pdf_info <- file.info(path)
  png_info <- file.info(png_path)
  needs_convert <- is.na(png_info$mtime) || (!is.na(pdf_info$mtime) && pdf_info$mtime > png_info$mtime)

  if (needs_convert) {
    pdftools::pdf_convert(
      pdf = path,
      format = "png",
      dpi = dpi,
      filenames = png_path
    )
  }

  png_path
}

# Overview

The CMAP module looks for CNA amplification/deletion events with similar cis and trans effects to known `r cmap_type_text` transription profiles from the [LINCS database](https://clue.io/GEO-guide). 
In order to do this, the algorithm first compiles a list of CNA features that are amplified or deleted in some number of samples. 
This list is then filtered to events with significant trans-regulatory effects-- more specifically, events where the amplified/deleted gene's CNA expression is significantly correlated with other genes' `r ome_type` expression. 
For each AMP/DEL event, these significant trans effects are compiled into a geneset (<code>`r sprintf("%s-cmap-%s-updn-genes.gmt", grp, typ)`</code>). 
These genesets are then used as queries to interrogate known `r cmap_type_text` transription profiles from the [LINCS database](https://clue.io/GEO-guide) 
and calculate weighted connectivity scores (WTCS), using the single-sample GSEA algorithm in `panoply_ssgsea`. 
Scores are normalized by perturbation and cell-type, and used in downstream analysis to more deeply investigate cis/trans effects of amplification and deletion events.

<!-- In order to calculate signficance, a permuation test is performed; 
for each amplification or deletion event, geneset(s) with a random selection of genes are generated (how many genes?). 
Knockdown profiles are also run against these genesets.  -->

For more information about the module please visit the [PANOPLY Wiki page](https://github.com/broadinstitute/PANOPLY/wiki/Data-Analysis-Modules%3A-panoply_cmap_analysis).


# Results


## Cis Regulated AMP/DEL Events

In order to identify amplification / deletion events of interest, the CMAP module first looks for events that also show, respectively, 
a negative / positive association with their `r cmap_type_text` profile.
Table `r tab_count` lists genes which, when amplified/deleted, are more likely to have a negative/positive outlier in the normalized enrichment score of their respective `r cmap_type_text` profile. 
<!-- Conversely, when deleted, are more likely to have a positive outlier NES.  -->
In other words, these are genes where the known `r cmap_type_text` profile mirrors the observed profile in samples with the AMP/DEL event.
If a gene mimics its `r cmap_type_text` profile for _both_ amplification and deletion events, it appears on the bi-directional list.

The reported FDR value is the expected ratio of false-to-true hits; false hits are calculated via an identical analysis on permuted datasets with randomly selected genesets for each amp/del event. 
The provided confidence interval assumes a poisson distribution for the number of hits. 

```{r import_sig_cis_effects, include=TRUE, echo=FALSE}
## Import CMAP Cis-Regulated Genes
df_sig_cis_uni = read.table(fn_sig_genes_uni, header = T) %>%
  group_by(gene) %>%
  summarise(direction = ifelse(n()==2, 'BOTH', direction), .groups = "drop")

## FDR information
# import and wrangle file
lines_sig_cis <- readr::read_lines(fn_sig_genes_fdr)
lines_sig_cis <- stringr::str_trim(lines_sig_cis) # prune start/end 
lines_sig_cis <- lines_sig_cis[lines_sig_cis != ""] # remove blank lines
# parse data
idx_section <- which(stringr::str_detect(lines_sig_cis, "^Genes CIS-enriched in ")) # get section headers
sig_genes_fdr <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(idx_section, function(i) {
  section_lines = lines_sig_cis[i:length(lines_sig_cis)]
  # parse FDR info from file
  section <- stringr::str_match(lines_sig_cis[i], "^Genes CIS-enriched in (.*):")[, 2] # get section title
  fdr_line <- section_lines[stringr::str_detect(section_lines, "^FDR:")][1] # get first FDR line (this will be the one for this section)
  fdr <- if (is.na(fdr_line)) NA_real_ else as.numeric(stringr::str_match(fdr_line, "^FDR:\\s*([0-9.]+)")[, 2]) # grab FDR value
  ci_low <- if (is.na(fdr_line)) NA_real_ else as.numeric(stringr::str_match(fdr_line, "\\[\\s*([0-9.]+)")[, 2]) # grab lower confidence-interval value
  ci_high <- if (is.na(fdr_line)) NA_real_ else as.numeric(stringr::str_match(fdr_line, ",\\s*([0-9.]+)\\s*\\]")[, 2]) # grab upper confidence-interval value
  # put it in a table format
  tibble::tibble(category = section, fdr = fdr, ci_low = ci_low, ci_high = ci_high
  )
}))
```

### Annotation Enrichment

Table `r tab_count` summarizes any annotations that are significantly enriched in samples with these amplification or deletion event. 
It contains significant results from overrepresentation analysis of sample metadata terms (e.g. clinical annotation, inferred phenotypes, etc.) in these samples. 
Shown are BH adjusted p-values derived from Fisher's exact test (<span style="background-color:#90ee90">p<0.01</span>, <span style="background-color:#ffff00">0.01<p<0.02</span>, <span style="background-color:#ffa500">0.02<p<0.05</span>). 
Full results can be found in  (<code>`r basename(fn_annot_enrich)`</code>)

```{r tab_annot_enrich, include=TRUE, echo=FALSE}
df_annot_enrich = read.csv(fn_annot_enrich)
df_annot_enrich_sig = filter(df_annot_enrich, adj.pvalue<fdr) %>%
  select(-fisher.test.pvalue) # drop nominal p-value

}

## Trans Effect of AMP/DEL Events

Figure `r fig_count` shows the overlap between trans effects identified by significant CNA-proteome correlation, 
and those identified as significant by CMAP.
A gene is considered to be a significant trans effect in the CMAP results if the normalized enrichment score for its `r cmap_type_text` profile is significant, relative to other genes for that that amp/del event.
The full list of significant trans genes identified by CMAP can be found in <code>`r sprintf("%s-cmap-%s-sig-genes-translist.gmt", grp, typ)`</code>.

```{r overlap_fig, include=TRUE, out.width='100%', out.height='100%', fig.pos='H', echo=FALSE, fig.cap=paste0('**Figure ', fig_count,'**: Overlap between CNA correlation trans-effects and significant CMAP trans effects.')}
knitr::include_graphics(prepare_figure_for_html(fn_overlap_fig))
```

## ssGSEA results

For significant AMP / DEL events, ssGSEA is performed on the global `r ome_type` to CNA correlation values for the event gene. Results are visualized below.

<!-- `create.ssgsea.dataset()` from cmap-annotate.R line 243 -->

```{r ssgsea_heatmap, echo=FALSE, include=FALSE}

n.max=cmap_yaml[["panoply_ssgsea_report"]]$top_n

## create the figure
ssgsea_gct = parse.gctx(fn_ssgsea_gct)
pw_hm(output.prefix=ssgsea_gct,
      fdr.max=fdr.max,
      n.max=n.max,

```

# Parameters

This section contains the parameters used to run the CMAP module.

<!-- Details about the parameters listed in **Table `r tab_count`** can be found in the [PANOPLY WIKI](https://github.com/broadinstitute/PANOPLY/wiki/Data-Analysis-Modules%3A-panoply_mo_nmf).     -->
    
```{r params, include=TRUE, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
yaml_section_to_tibble <- function(lst, section_name) {
  format_leaf <- function(x) {
    if (is.null(x)) return("NULL")
    if (length(x) == 0) return("")
    if (is.atomic(x) && !is.list(x)) {
      if (length(x) == 1) return(as.character(x))
      return(paste(as.character(x), collapse = ", "))
    }
    paste(utils::capture.output(utils::str(x, max.level = 4, give.attr = FALSE)), collapse = "\n")
  }

  flatten <- function(node, path) {
    if (is.null(node)) {
      return(tibble::tibble(param = path, value = "NULL"))
    }
    if (is.atomic(node) && !is.list(node)) {
      return(tibble::tibble(param = path, value = format_leaf(node)))
    }
    if (!is.list(node)) {
      return(tibble::tibble(param = path, value = format_leaf(node)))
    }

    nm <- names(node)
    if (is.null(nm) || all(nm == "")) {
      return(dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(node), function(i) {
        p <- if (nzchar(path)) paste0(path, "[[", i, "]]") else paste0("[[", i, "]]")
        flatten(node[[i]], p)
      })))
    }

    dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(nm, function(n) {
      p <- if (nzchar(path)) paste0(path, ".", n) else n
      flatten(node[[n]], p)
    }))
  }

  if (is.null(lst) || length(lst) == 0) {
    return(tibble::tibble(
      yaml_section = character(0),
      param = character(0),
      value = character(0)
    ))
  }

  out <- flatten(lst, "")
  dplyr::mutate(out, yaml_section = section_name, .before = 1)
}

tab_param <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  yaml_section_to_tibble(cmap_yaml[["panoply_cmap_analysis"]], "panoply_cmap_analysis"),
  yaml_section_to_tibble(cmap_yaml[["DEV_directory_and_file_names"]], "DEV_directory_and_file_names")
)

DT::datatable(
  tab_param,
  rownames = FALSE,
  colnames = c("YAML section", "Parameter", "Value"),

        "<code>panoply_cmap_analysis</code> and <code>DEV_directory_and_file_names</code>."
      )
    )
  ),
  options = list(
    pageLength = 25,
    lengthMenu = c(10, 25, 50, 100),
    autoWidth = TRUE,
    # order = list(list(0, "asc"), list(1, "asc")),
    dom = "lfrtip"
  )
) %>%
  DT::formatStyle(columns = names(tab_param), fontSize = "13px")
```
